text:
Anya: heads-up — nightly bench (seqlen=512 mix) shows p99 token latency +18% on nodes running the new kernel-picker (commit ab12cd). p50 is flat. Observed a repeating pattern: latency spikes correlated with KV-cache block swaps across GQA/MQA paths.

Ryan: can you paste the bench id + sample logs? is this reproducible locally?

Anya: bench id 2026-03-17-gqa-mix, repro on canary cluster A (a100-48g). snippet from worker logs:```
[2026-03-17T07:14:02Z] pick_kernel: chosen=gqa_paged_block v=0.71 seqlen=512 kv_layout=kvstripe blocks=[0,1]
[2026-03-17T07:14:02Z] pick_kernel: chosen=mqa_paged_block v=0.65 seqlen=64 kv_layout=kvstripe blocks=[2,3]
[2026-03-17T07:14:02Z] kvcache: block_swap triggered, evict=0 alloc=2 frag=0.32
[2026-03-17T07:14:02Z] kernel_launch: gqa_paged_block latency=3.2ms
[2026-03-17T07:14:02Z] kernel_launch: mqa_paged_block latency=3.0ms
```
Pattern: we flip kernel implementations mid-request stream because the picker sees different block alignments at different seq prefixes. That causes warmups and KV re-layout thrash.

Marco: interesting — sounds like picker hysteresis is too low when kv stripe fragmentation crosses the decision boundary. Did the autotuner change thresholds?

Ciara: last night autotuner ran a sweep that relaxed seqlen thresholds for small-batch MQA, but it also dropped the kv_block_size heuristic from 64->32 for cache compaction experiments. Could be related.

Ryan: can we reproduce with a controlled profile? i.e., synthetic workload with alternating long/short seqlens to force block misalignment. I can spin up a local runner.

Anya: yes, repro script attached in thread gist: https://gist.redwood/dev/gqa-mqa-kvstripe-repro (private). Quick run: python ./repro.py --pattern=alternating --iters=500 --batch=8 --seed=42

perf-bot: regression alert: nightly-p99-gqa-path increased by 17.9% (baseline 2.71ms -> 3.20ms). Affected nodes: canary-A (a100-48g). Related commit: ab12cd.

Marco: I ran a profiler on the repro for 200 iters. flame snippet:```
CPU: kernel_picker.evaluate (35%)
GPU: gqa_paged_block (40% warmup stalls), mqa_paged_block (20%)
KV-cache ops: block_migrate (12%), eviction_scan (8%)
```
Warmup stalls mean the chosen kernel path frequently had cold KV stripes that triggered fragment copy.

Ciara: hypothesis: when kv_block_size was reduced to 32, small seqlen MQA picks align to different block indices compared to GQA picks. That increases interleaving and causes more frequent block_swaps. The picker sees different per-request latency models and flips.

Ryan: quick mitigation ideas: 1) increase picker hysteresis on block index differences, 2) pin kernel by request group for N requests to avoid oscillation, 3) revert kv_block_size change. Which is least disruptive?

Anya: reverting block_size is simplest and immediate. Pinning across requests could reduce tail but may hurt cache utilization. Hysteresis seems safest long-term.

Marco: I pushed a quick toggle flag to runtime: kernel_picker.hysteresis_blocks = 2 (default 0). Deploy-bot just reports canary deploy below. We should run repro again.

deploy-bot: canary deployed commit 9f3b7a to cluster canary-A (runtime toggle: kernel_picker.hysteresis_blocks=2).

Anya: reran repro 10m after deploy: p99 dropped back to 2.78ms (improved). Results:```
before: p99=3.20ms p50=0.86ms
after:  p99=2.78ms p50=0.85ms
block_swap_rate: before=0.42/s after=0.07/s
```
Good signal but need broader sweep.

Ciara: i'll schedule an autotune sweep with the hysteresis param in the matrix (values: 0,1,2,4) plus kv_block_size values [32,48,64] and run on canary-A and canary-B. Also include mixed seqlen workloads (alternating, bursty, steady).

Ryan: i want a small change in the picker scoring function: add a cost penalty when predicted block_swap_rate > 0.2. We can compute an approximate rate from recent kvcache EWMAs. That should bias away from oscillatory picks even if raw latency models favor the alternate kernel. I can prototype in picker core.

Marco: sounds good. If we add penalty, ensure fallback when block_swap prediction is stale. Also add a feature flag so we can A/B.

Anya: next steps summary: (1) run Ciara's sweep and collect p99, block_swap_rate, kernel_switch_count. (2) Ryan prototypes penalty-based scoring + FF. (3) if sweep shows hysteresis=2 works globally, we roll. (4) consider reverting kv_block_size change if anomalies persist.

perf-bot: noted — creating regression ticket RW-PR-4763 and attaching nightly artifact set.

Ciara: i'll attach the sweep plan, plus the repro logs and the profiler traces to the ticket.

Anya: thanks all — keeping this thread as ground truth for the investigation. Ping me if you need cluster creds or logs. :thumbsup:
